One created and maintained by people, e.g. a maize field, a pine plantation, an orchard or a fish pond.
Natural ecosystems have high diversity and complex, stable food webs; artificial ones have low diversity and simple, unstable webs.
Falling soil fertility, pest and disease outbreaks, more chemical use, loss of habitats, bare erodible soil.
Holds the topsoil, retains water (rain soaks in), reduces evaporation, adds organic matter.
Bare soil, erosion, gullies, weak animals. Cure: destocking and rotational grazing.

front: How is erosion on sloping fields reduced?
back: Contour ploughing and contour ridges, which slow water and lead it away safely.
Riverbank erosion, siltation of rivers and dams, mercury pollution, open pits.
notes: Cures: regulation, refilling and replanting, mercury-free methods.

front: Why are frequent veld fires harmful?
back: They destroy ground cover, young trees and organic matter, leave soil bare and release carbon dioxide.

front: How do you find the carrying capacity of grazing land?
back: Carrying capacity (animals) = area of grazing ÷ area needed per animal.
